title: Week 2 Mastery Quiz · Evidence, Methodology, and Academic Integrity

questions.question: A student paraphrases three sentences from a report but cites only the agency name, not the exact report. What repair makes the claim auditable?
options: Citing the department homepage adequately identifies any report issued there.
Identify the specific report, authoring body, year, page or section, and traceable quotation context
Citing the report's title without edition, date, or relevant section fully documents the paraphrase.
A bibliography entry alone guarantees that the paraphrase accurately represents the source.
questions.explanation: Identify the specific report, authoring body, year, page or section, and traceable quotation context

questions.question: Fictional research notebook: the data table shows 23 interviews, but the methodology describes 30. Which first response protects integrity?
options: Reconcile exclusions and missing records in a dated methods note before drawing conclusions
Silently change the table to 30
Keep both counts without discussion
Delete the methodology
questions.explanation: Reconcile exclusions and missing records in a dated methods note before drawing conclusions

questions.question: An analyst compares a government press release and a watchdog report on the same election. How should their disagreement be investigated?
options: Average their conclusions
Assume the watchdog is always correct
Ignore primary records
Compare each document's evidence, methods, dates, definitions, and independently verifiable claims
questions.explanation: Compare each document's evidence, methods, dates, definitions, and independently verifiable claims

questions.question: A fictional school survey recruits respondents through a voluntary public link. Which limitation belongs beside its results?
options: No limitation because the link is public
Its exact sampling bias is zero
Volunteer and access biases limit population-wide claims
Every public survey is fraudulent
questions.explanation: Volunteer and access biases limit population-wide claims

questions.question: A student uses an AI tool to outline an argument, then verifies every cited document independently. Which disclosure is academically appropriate?
options: Present the outline as entirely unaided
Disclose the tool's assistance and independently verify sources and final reasoning
List the AI tool as author of every historical source
Omit all citations
questions.explanation: Disclose the tool's assistance and independently verify sources and final reasoning

questions.question: A case study relies on confidential interviews. Which protocol best protects participants and the reliability of evidence?
options: Publish identifying transcripts automatically
Claim anonymity while saving full names publicly
Collect information without consent
Obtain appropriate consent, minimize identifiers, safeguard notes, and disclose methods without exposing identities
questions.explanation: Obtain appropriate consent, minimize identifiers, safeguard notes, and disclose methods without exposing identities

questions.question: Simulated archive log: Document A is dated 2018; Document B quotes it but is dated 2016. What should the researcher do?
options: Flag the chronology conflict and verify the document dates and editions
Assume the quotation proves the earlier date
Discard all records from both years
Rewrite the document date silently
questions.explanation: Flag the chronology conflict and verify the document dates and editions

questions.question: A report finds a statistical relationship between youth voting and school completion. Which study design would better examine competing explanations?
options: One more anecdote
A campaign slogan
A pre-specified analysis controlling for relevant confounders and examining alternative mechanisms
Only a vocabulary quiz
questions.explanation: A pre-specified analysis controlling for relevant confounders and examining alternative mechanisms

questions.question: A source is an official budget table but does not specify whether amounts are nominal or inflation-adjusted. What is the defensible inference?
options: Its change over time is fully explained
The table needs currency basis, coverage, and price adjustment clarified before real-trend claims
Official sources have no limitations
Inflation has no relationship to public budgets
questions.explanation: The table needs currency basis, coverage, and price adjustment clarified before real-trend claims

questions.question: A senior changes the interpretation of a treaty after locating a newer authenticated translation. What should the research notebook preserve?
options: Only the replacement claim
Neither version
A revised title without evidence
Earlier interpretation, changed passage, translation provenance, date, and reason for revision
questions.explanation: Earlier interpretation, changed passage, translation provenance, date, and reason for revision

shortResponse: What procedures make research credible, ethical, reproducible, and honest?
rubric: 10 points: precise claim (2), accurate concepts (2), two specific pieces of evidence (2), reasoning (2), counterargument or limitation (1), revision condition (1).
